recipes.name: Swiss Vegetable Medley
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package frozen mixed vegetables, thawed
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Set aside 1/4 cup of cheese, and 1/4 cup of onions.
In a medium-size mixing bowl, combine thawed vegetables, mushroom soup, 3/4 cup Swiss cheese, sour cream, remaining fried onions, and pepper. Pour ingredients into a 2 quart casserole dish.
Bake for 30 minutes. Sprinkle reserved cheese and onions on top of the casserole and bake additional 5 minutes, or until the cheese has melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Swiss Vegetable Medley
raw_recipe.description: Great dish when you are tired of the same old thing. I always get asked for the recipe if I bring it to a potluck. I usually use the frozen bag of mixed broccoli, cauliflower and carrots.

review.reviewBody: I, too, have made this for years. I like cheddar cheese better than Swiss and I use a small can (2.8 oz) of fried onion rings (not 6 oz. as listed). Also, I add about 1/4 cup milk with sour cream to keep casserole from getting too sticky. Also, always make sure veggies are thawed or they don't get done.

Good recipe added 1/4 milk to sour cream. Added small can of sliced mushrooms and used 1 cup of Cabot shredded seriously sharp cheese. Layered sliced Swiss on top of mixture and baked as directed. Added French’s onion after 30 minutes bake time for 5 minutes. Turned out very tasty. Replacing my previous recipe.

I made this recipe for our work Christmas potluck. I doubled the recipe, and added garlic and onion powder and cooked it in the crock pot on high for 3 1/2 hours. Delish!!! Next time I will add mushrooms just for something extra.

This was a five star recipe with a few additions....a little milk to thin out the sauce, fresh garlic, season salt, regular salt, pepper, 1 jar pimentos, cheddar cheese instead of swiss, and mixing some fried onions into the veggies as well as sprinkling them on top. I used a California blend for the veggies and 2 cans of green beans.

Yummy !! I used the California mix veggies with cauliflower, broccoli and carrots and I used reduced fat Swiss cheese (put in a little extra, couldn't resist ;) and low fat sour cream. I only used about half the 6 oz can of onions. I made it for New Years Day dinner and everyone loved it! I definitely plan on making it again. Oh and it's easy! That makes it even better :)

Very good. I used frozen veggies and steamed first, made the sauce and refrigerated until just before time to go to a potluck. As others, used shredded colby-Jack cheese. Before adding the sauce sprinkled steamed, drained veggies with Mrs. Dash seasoning for extra flavor. Did not have the onion rings and just sprinkled extra cheese on top. No doubt the onion rings would add even more flavor and texture. Will try that next time. Thanks for an easy, quick and different vegetable dish.

I always substitute sharp cheddar instead of swiss, and I use mayo instead of sour cream. Once in a while I'll top it with crunchy chow mein noodles to be different. This is my go to for a pot luck contribution.

I have made this recipe for years and the crowd loves it. Making it as presented creates a VERY RICH recipe. In fact, most people feel guilty about eating it and while they love the blend of flavors they think they may have a heart attack.
Seriously, it is that rich!
Here's the remedy for a wonderful side dish that folks can relax and enjoy. It's so simple too! Double the veggies! The sauce is so rich, there's plenty to go around and you can even feel good about eating your veggies. Everyone can relax :D Oh and by the way, I often use a blend of fresh and frozen veggies. The bags of frozen are super convenient but the quality can vary and I tend to buy store brands which are not always great so I go with some fresh as well.
Great recipe, but I also add one small jar of diced pimentos, drained. Great for color and flavor. Absolutely delicious with a standing rib roast.

Excellent recipe although I forgot to reserve some cheese for the top. And I reduced the sour cream by half only because that's all I had. However, in future I will keep to the reduced amount as I don't see the need for more. The flavor was great. It makes serves a lot more than the 5 the recipe states. Will be using this recipe again.

I love Monterey Jack cheese, it melts so good, so I use that

instead of swiss. Other than that everyone LOVES this casserole! I bring it everywhere.
I made this and doubled it for a potluck. It was good-but not great. Worth making one time. Thank you for the recipe!! :)
My family loves this dish! Always a must during the holidays.
Used chicken noodle soup instead of mushroom, used oyster crackers and shredded Mexican cheese, used several spices, delicious
LOVE THIS, WILL MAKE AGAIN
Tested a couple week back will definitely be making for Thanksgiving.
I added Carrots and some Brussel Sprouts and a little onion. Delish!

I use cream of chicken soup instead mushroom soup. Delish!! 
I make this all the time...great for the holidays!!
I make it every Thanksgiving
I make this every holiday its a family favorite .. I make it just as written !!! :)
